title: Transferring RL Gains from a Weaker Teacher
question: Supervising a student's own rollouts token by token, choose what to transfer from the teacher — its distribution, or the change reasoning tuning made to it.
elab:
On-policy distillation supervises a student on its own sampled tokens. A teacher's RL-tuning delta relative to its pre-RL reference can transfer useful reasoning even when the teacher is weaker than the student; this task designs that per-token signal for one weaker-teacher distillation run, scored on three held-out math benchmarks.

On-policy distillation trains a student on its own rollouts and supervises each token with a frozen teacher; the usual signal is the teacher's log-probability minus the student's. Recent work argues that is the wrong quantity — what should transfer is not the teacher's distribution but the change post-training made to it, visible by also holding the teacher's own pre-post-training base. The task asks for the per-token signal in the regime where that difference matters most: the teacher is weaker than the student (a small post-trained model teaching a larger one), so imitating the teacher pulls the student toward a worse model while its post-training delta can still help. One distillation run is scored on three held-out math benchmarks. It matters because on-policy distillation is now the standard way reasoning ability is moved between models, and the signal is its core.
readme_settings_line: Qwen3-1.7B student / weaker Qwen3-0.6B teacher · MATH-500; Same checkpoint · AMC23 (avg@8); Same checkpoint · OlympiadBench.
readme_methods_line: OPD² (Heo et al., 2026); ExOPD (Yang et al., 2026); Raw teacher-reference delta; Teacher-student OPD (Heo et al., 2026); Constant advantage / self-SFT.
description_md:
# Per-token training signal for on-policy distillation

## The question

On-policy distillation trains a student on **its own** rollouts and supervises
them token by token with a frozen teacher. The usual signal is the teacher's
log-probability of the sampled token minus the student's (T − S). A 2026 line of
work argues that this is the wrong quantity: what you want to transfer is not the
teacher's distribution but the *change* reasoning tuning made to it, which you
can see by also holding a frozen **reference** model — the checkpoint the teacher
was tuned from — and looking at the difference between the two (T − R).

This task is scoped to that second regime: **transferring the teacher's
post-training delta, T − R, where R is the teacher's own base.** The claim under
test is that the delta transfers reasoning even when the teacher is **not
stronger** than the student: it carries the change post-training made, not an
absolute teacher-vs-student comparison. A pure T − S signal, by contrast, is
classic distillation — it pulls the student toward the teacher itself, and only
helps when the teacher is the better model.

So in **every** setting the teacher is **weaker than the student**: a smaller
post-trained model, scored below the student on the held-out benchmarks, with
the frozen reference being that teacher's own pre-post-training base. A T − S
signal therefore pulls the student toward a worse model and is expected to land
at or near the do-nothing baseline, while a good delta signal should still
improve the student. The settings score the same distilled student on
different held-out problems of the domain it is trained on, one held-out
benchmark per setting.

Given the student's own rollout and what all three models assign to each
sampled token, **what per-token training signal built on the teacher's
post-training delta transfers reasoning best from a teacher that is weaker than
its student?**

That is the whole task. The rollout, the three forward passes, the PPO-clipped
policy-gradient update and the optimizer are fixed; you write the function that
turns the log-probabilities into the dense per-token advantage.

*Sibling task.* `llm-on-policy-distillation` is the regime-1 object — classic
on-policy distillation from a stronger teacher, a pure T − S signal over the full
logit surface. This task is the regime-2 object: the teacher is never stronger
than the student, the estimator is over the student's own sampled token (plus
top-K expectations), and it has the frozen reference model that regime-1 does
not. Keep the two distinct.

## Your surface

One function, in `opd2/src/open_r1/trainers/custom_token_signal.py`:

```python
def compute_per_token_signal(
    student_lp, teacher_lp, teacher_base_lp,
    mean_student_lp, mean_teacher_lp, mean_teacher_base_lp,
    completion_mask, solutions, step, total_steps,
) -> torch.Tensor:          # [B, T] float
```

All six tensors are `[B, T]` float32 on the same device, aligned to the
student's own sampled tokens. Writing `S`, `T`, `R` for the student, the
teacher and the frozen reference, all log-probabilities normalised over the
full vocabulary at the training temperature:

| argument | meaning |
|---|---|
| `student_lp` | `S(t) = log p_student(y_t \| prompt, y_<t)` at the token the student actually sampled |
| `teacher_lp` | `T(t)`, the same token under the frozen teacher |
| `teacher_base_lp` | `R(t)`, the same token under the frozen reference the teacher was tuned from |
| `mean_student_lp` | `E_{v~p_student}[ log p_student(v) ]` — the expectation is over the student's own next-token distribution, truncated to its top-K columns |
| `mean_teacher_lp` | `E_{v~p_student}[ log p_teacher(v) ]` |
| `mean_teacher_base_lp` | `E_{v~p_student}[ log p_reference(v) ]` |
| `completion_mask` | `[B, T]` bool. True on real sampled tokens; False on padding and on rollouts the harness has already rejected. Values at False positions are zeros and are discarded afterwards — but any reduction you take across tokens or across the batch has to respect it. |
| `solutions` | `list[str]`, length `B`: the **training** set's own reference answer for each prompt. Training data, not evaluation data. |
| `step`, `total_steps` | 0-based optimizer step and the total for this run, so a schedule is expressible. |

Return `[B, T]`, same shape as `student_lp`. Larger means *make this token more
likely*. Non-finite entries are zeroed for you. A wrong shape or a non-tensor
return raises rather than being silently coerced.

## Fixed, and not reachable from here

The rollout and its sampling parameters; the three frozen forward passes and
the top-K gather that produces the expectations; the PPO clip and the
ratio-vs-old-logprob machinery; the masking of padding and of degenerate
rollouts; the constant the signal is multiplied by before it enters the loss;
the optimizer, the learning-rate schedule, the step budget and the checkpoint
that is saved. The student and both frozen models are fixed. You cannot change
the state distribution — only what is said about the states the student visits.
The **gradient path** is fixed with it: this surface is a policy-gradient signal
over the student's own *sampled* tokens, not direct-backprop distribution
matching over the full vocabulary — a full-logit or teacher-top-K objective is a
different surface and lives in the sibling task `llm-distill-sgo-objective`.

## Reference baselines

The delta family, a pure-T−S baseline, and a null — expressed on exactly this
surface, ported from `naver-ai/opd2` at commit `2dac53fb` (Apache-2.0) and the
G-OPD paper below. The three delta-family arms are what a regime-2 contribution
must beat; they should all beat the null in every setting.

**delta_raw** — the raw RL-delta, T − R, at the sampled token: the teacher minus
its own pre-RL reference, no correction, no gating. The clean regime-2 anchor
(and the shipped starter). It is the delta term of OPD², before centring and
gating. Heo, Hwang, Yun & Han, *On-Policy Delta Distillation*, arXiv:2607.15161.

```python
return teacher_lp - teacher_base_lp
```

**ExOPD** — reward extrapolation past the teacher: scale the RL-delta by λ > 1
and subtract the student's own gap to the reference. Yang, Liu, Xie, Yang, Yang &
Lin, *Learning beyond Teacher: Generalized On-Policy Distillation with Reward
Extrapolation*, arXiv:2602.12125; λ = 1.25 is upstream's default, after
`src/open_r1/trainers/exopd_trainer.py`.

```python
lam = 1.25
return lam * (teacher_lp - teacher_base_lp) - (student_lp - teacher_base_lp)
```

**OPD²** — the delta signal, centred under the student's own distribution and
gated by the direction plain OPD would move. Heo et al., arXiv:2607.15161,
after `src/open_r1/trainers/opd2_trainer.py`.

```python
signal = (teacher_lp - teacher_base_lp) - (mean_teacher_lp - mean_teacher_base_lp)
d_base = (teacher_lp - student_lp)      - (mean_teacher_lp - mean_student_lp)
return torch.where((signal * d_base) < 0, torch.zeros_like(signal), signal)
```

**OPD (T − S) — not a delta-family method.** Plain on-policy
distillation: the teacher-minus-student log-prob at the sampled token, with no
reference model. This is classic distillation from a stronger teacher (the
regime-1 signal), included as a baseline: with a teacher weaker than the student
it has nothing better to pull toward, so it is expected to sit at or near the
do-nothing baseline and to lag the delta family. That is the point being
measured, not a defect. Heo et al., arXiv:2607.15161 ("OPD" column),
`src/open_r1/trainers/opd_trainer.py`.

```python
return teacher_lp - student_lp
```

**null** — a constant signal, carrying no teacher or reference information at
all. It reduces the fixed update to on-policy self-SFT (entropy minimisation on
the student's own rollouts), a strong self-improvement baseline on a capable
student; the delta family must beat it wherever the signal is real.

All are unrefereed 2026 preprints or simple baselines; treat their ordering as a
hypothesis to test, not as ground truth. The papers report the delta family
above a pure-T−S signal above the untouched student — but only with a teacher
stronger than the student, on students several times larger than the one here
and on a substantially larger training budget. The weaker-teacher direction
scored here is not one they run.

## Metric

Held-out accuracy of the distilled student, one held-out benchmark of the
reasoning domain it is trained on per setting; every setting scores the same
distilled student. Higher is better. What is measured is whether your per-token
signal transfers reasoning to unseen problems, not whether it was tuned to a
configuration you were handed.

You are working inside `/workspace`. The package source tree
`/workspace/opd2/` is the research scaffold for this task.
instruction_harness.Files You May Edit:
You may **only** modify these files, and **only within the listed line ranges
(inclusive, 1-indexed)**.

Editing outside those ranges will score your submission zero, and so will
creating or deleting any file inside the task's own source trees
(`/workspace/opd2/`, and anything else that was already there when
you started). Files you write anywhere else — scratch space, caches,
checkpoints, `$OUTPUT_DIR`, `/tmp` — are not part of your submission, so use
them freely.

- `opd2/src/open_r1/trainers/custom_token_signal.py`
- editable lines **70–76**


Other files you may **read** for context (do not modify):
- `opd2/src/open_r1/trainers/mls_signal_trainer.py`
- `opd2/src/open_r1/trainers/opd_trainer.py`
instruction_harness.How You Will Be Evaluated:
After you finish, evaluation runs a fixed set of scripts and aggregates the
metrics they emit into one score, the same way the leaderboard does. Those
scripts are **not** in your workspace: you cannot read or modify them.

Which settings you are scored on is deliberately **not** disclosed, and some
of them never run where you can see them. In Harbor you can re-run the
evaluation, so naming the settings and their budgets would turn this into a
targeting exercise; what is being measured is whether the change you submit
is a *general* improvement to the algorithm, not whether it was tuned to a
configuration you were handed.
instruction_harness.Parameter Budget: Keep your model's total parameter count at or below the strongest reference baseline's. A check runs automatically — you don't need to invoke it — and a materially larger model makes the run invalid. The contribution must be algorithmic, not extra capacity.
instruction_harness.Tips:
- Keep the function/class signatures of the editable regions identical;
  evaluation imports them by name.
- Determinism matters: seeds are fixed; don't introduce hidden randomness.
- The baseline implementations above are deliberately strong. Aim for an
  *algorithmic* improvement — many hyperparameters are locked outside the
  editable surface anyway.
instruction_harness.Time Budget:
You have **5 hours** of wall-clock time before submission, covering
everything you do here: reading the code, editing it, and any trial runs
you launch.

Good luck.

baselines.name: OPD² (Heo et al., 2026)
baselines.docstring:
OPD2 baseline — the delta signal with expectation correction and gating.

Port of `OPD2Trainer._compute_opd_rewards` in naver-ai/opd2 @2dac53fb
(`src/open_r1/trainers/opd2_trainer.py:314-324`), the paper's headline method
(Heo, Hwang, Yun & Han, *On-Policy Delta Distillation*, arXiv:2607.15161,
Tables 2-3, column "OPD2"):

    signal  = (eval_gt - tb_gt)  - (E_base[eval] - E_base[tb])
    d_base  = (eval_gt - base_gt) - (E_base[eval] - E_base[base])
    per_token_signal = 0 where signal * d_base < 0, else signal
    per_token_signal -= opd_rewards_bias                  # default 0.0

The delta `(teacher - reference)` is what the paper calls the delta signal: the
part of the teacher that reasoning tuning put there.  The `E_base[.]` terms
centre it under the student's own next-token distribution (upstream calls this
"pre_centering", always on), and the sign gate drops tokens where the delta
points against the direction plain OPD would move.

The expectations are taken over the student's top-K columns, K = 1024
(`opd2_rewards_top_k`, `configs.py:373`); the fixed pipeline computes them and
hands them in, so this file just reads them.

"""OPD2 baseline — the delta signal with expectation correction and gating.

Port of `OPD2Trainer._compute_opd_rewards` in naver-ai/opd2 @2dac53fb
(`src/open_r1/trainers/opd2_trainer.py:314-324`), the paper's headline method
(Heo, Hwang, Yun & Han, *On-Policy Delta Distillation*, arXiv:2607.15161,
Tables 2-3, column "OPD2"):

    signal  = (eval_gt - tb_gt)  - (E_base[eval] - E_base[tb])
    d_base  = (eval_gt - base_gt) - (E_base[eval] - E_base[base])
    per_token_signal = 0 where signal * d_base < 0, else signal
    per_token_signal -= opd_rewards_bias                  # default 0.0

The delta `(teacher - reference)` is what the paper calls the delta signal: the
part of the teacher that reasoning tuning put there.  The `E_base[.]` terms
centre it under the student's own next-token distribution (upstream calls this
"pre_centering", always on), and the sign gate drops tokens where the delta
points against the direction plain OPD would move.

The expectations are taken over the student's top-K columns, K = 1024
(`opd2_rewards_top_k`, `configs.py:373`); the fixed pipeline computes them and
hands them in, so this file just reads them.
"""

_FILE = "opd2/src/open_r1/trainers/custom_token_signal.py"

_BODY = """\
    # OPD2 (Heo et al. 2026, arXiv:2607.15161; opd2_trainer.py:314-324).
    # type-18 signal with pre-centering always on (mean_ratio == 1).
    signal = (teacher_lp - teacher_base_lp) - (mean_teacher_lp - mean_teacher_base_lp)
    d_base = (teacher_lp - student_lp) - (mean_teacher_lp - mean_student_lp)
    signal = torch.where(
        (signal * d_base) < 0, torch.zeros_like(signal), signal
    )
    return signal
"""

OPS = [
    {
        "op": "replace",
        "file": _FILE,
        "start_line": 70,
        "end_line": 76,
        "content": _BODY,
    },
]

-    #
-    # Starter: the raw delta between the teacher and the model it was tuned

+    )
+    return signal
     # END EDITABLE REGION

"""Per-token training signal for on-policy distillation (EDITABLE).

The fixed pipeline samples a rollout from the student, then runs three frozen
forward passes over that rollout and hands you, for every sampled token, what
each model thinks of it.  Your job is to turn those numbers into the dense
per-token advantage the GRPO update is driven by.

Symbols used below (all log-probabilities, all at temperature `temperature`,
all normalised over the full vocabulary):

    S(t)   = log p_student(y_t | prompt, y_<t)     the student's own rollout
    T(t)   = log p_teacher(y_t | prompt, y_<t)     frozen reasoning-tuned teacher
    R(t)   = log p_reference(y_t | prompt, y_<t)   frozen model the teacher was tuned FROM

and the three expectations under the student's own next-token distribution,
truncated to the student's top-K columns (K is fixed by the harness):

    E[S](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_student(v)
    E[T](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_teacher(v)
    E[R](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_reference(v)

What is fixed and NOT reachable from here: the rollout itself, the three
forward passes, the top-K gather, the PPO clip, the masking of padding and of
degenerate rollouts, the constant the signal is multiplied by before it enters
the loss, the optimizer, the schedule and the checkpoint that is saved.
"""
import torch


def compute_per_token_signal(
    student_lp: torch.Tensor,
    teacher_lp: torch.Tensor,
    teacher_base_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_student_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_teacher_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_teacher_base_lp: torch.Tensor,
    completion_mask: torch.Tensor,
    solutions: list,
    step: int,
    total_steps: int,
) -> torch.Tensor:

    signal = (teacher_lp - teacher_base_lp) - (mean_teacher_lp - mean_teacher_base_lp)

baselines.docstring:
ExOPD baseline — reward extrapolation past the teacher.

Port of `ExOPDTrainer._compute_opd_rewards` in naver-ai/opd2 @2dac53fb
(`src/open_r1/trainers/exopd_trainer.py:222-229`), the paper's ExOPD arm
(arXiv:2607.15161, Tables 2-3, column "ExOPD").  The method itself is the
reward-extrapolation instantiation of G-OPD: Yang, Liu, Xie, Yang, Yang & Lin,
*Learning beyond Teacher: Generalized On-Policy Distillation with Reward
Extrapolation*, arXiv:2602.12125.

    per_token_signal = lambda * (eval_gt - tb_gt) - (base_gt - tb_gt)
    if lambda > 1.5:  per_token_signal /= lambda        # scale guard
    per_token_signal -= opd_rewards_bias                # default 0.0

lambda = 1.25 is upstream's default (`configs.py:335`) and the value every
shipped recipe uses.  lambda = 1 would recover OPD exactly; lambda > 1 amplifies
the teacher's own specialisation over its base.  The `lambda > 1.5` guard is
inert at 1.25 and is kept only so this file is a faithful transcription.

"""ExOPD baseline — reward extrapolation past the teacher.

(`src/open_r1/trainers/exopd_trainer.py:222-229`), the paper's ExOPD arm

*Learning beyond Teacher: Generalized On-Policy Distillation with Reward
Extrapolation*, arXiv:2602.12125.

    per_token_signal = lambda * (eval_gt - tb_gt) - (base_gt - tb_gt)
    if lambda > 1.5:  per_token_signal /= lambda        # scale guard

"""Per-token training signal for on-policy distillation (EDITABLE).

The fixed pipeline samples a rollout from the student, then runs three frozen
forward passes over that rollout and hands you, for every sampled token, what
each model thinks of it.  Your job is to turn those numbers into the dense
per-token advantage the GRPO update is driven by.

Symbols used below (all log-probabilities, all at temperature `temperature`,
all normalised over the full vocabulary):

    S(t)   = log p_student(y_t | prompt, y_<t)     the student's own rollout
    T(t)   = log p_teacher(y_t | prompt, y_<t)     frozen reasoning-tuned teacher
    R(t)   = log p_reference(y_t | prompt, y_<t)   frozen model the teacher was tuned FROM

and the three expectations under the student's own next-token distribution,
truncated to the student's top-K columns (K is fixed by the harness):

    E[S](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_student(v)
    E[T](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_teacher(v)
    E[R](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_reference(v)

What is fixed and NOT reachable from here: the rollout itself, the three
forward passes, the top-K gather, the PPO clip, the masking of padding and of
degenerate rollouts, the constant the signal is multiplied by before it enters
the loss, the optimizer, the schedule and the checkpoint that is saved.
"""
import torch


def compute_per_token_signal(
    student_lp: torch.Tensor,
    teacher_lp: torch.Tensor,
    teacher_base_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_student_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_teacher_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_teacher_base_lp: torch.Tensor,
    completion_mask: torch.Tensor,
    solutions: list,
    step: int,
    total_steps: int,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Return the dense per-token advantage for one batch of rollouts.

    Args:
        student_lp:           [B, T] float32, S(t).
        teacher_lp:           [B, T] float32, T(t).
        teacher_base_lp:      [B, T] float32, R(t).
        mean_student_lp:      [B, T] float32, E[S](t).
        mean_teacher_lp:      [B, T] float32, E[T](t).
        mean_teacher_base_lp: [B, T] float32, E[R](t).
        completion_mask:      [B, T] bool. True on real sampled tokens; False on
                              padding and on every position of a rollout the
                              harness has already rejected.  Values at False
                              positions are zeros and are discarded afterwards,
                              so you never have to mask your output -- but you
                              DO have to respect the mask in any reduction you
                              take across tokens or across the batch.
        solutions:            list[str] of length B, the training set's own
                              reference answer for each prompt.  Training data,
                              not evaluation data.
        step:                 optimizer step index, 0-based.
        total_steps:          total optimizer steps in this run.

    Returns:
        [B, T] float tensor, same shape as `student_lp`.  Larger means "make
        this token more likely".  Non-finite entries are zeroed by the harness.
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # EDITABLE REGION
    # ExOPD (G-OPD reward extrapolation; Yang et al. arXiv:2602.12125, as
    # implemented in exopd_trainer.py:222-229).  lambda = 1.25 is upstream's
    # default and the value in every shipped recipe.
    lam = 1.25
    signal = lam * (teacher_lp - teacher_base_lp) - (student_lp - teacher_base_lp)

        signal = signal / lam
    return signal
    # END EDITABLE REGION
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

baselines.name: Raw teacher-reference delta
baselines.docstring:
delta_raw baseline — the pure RL-delta, the clean regime-2 anchor.

This is the raw teacher-minus-reference log-prob at the student's own sampled
token: T - R, where R is the teacher's OWN pre-RL base model (Qwen3-4B-Base) and
T is the RL-post-trained teacher (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507).  It transfers the
CHANGE that reasoning tuning made to the teacher, and carries no absolute
teacher-vs-student comparison at all -- so, by regime-2's hypothesis, it should
help regardless of the teacher-student capability gap, and it must beat the
EM-FT null in every setting.

It is exactly the shipped starter body (`custom_template.py`), so it is the
zero-new-code anchor for the family: opd2 adds pre-centering and a sign gate on
top of this, exopd adds a lambda>1 mixture with the (S-R) term on top of this.
Contrast `opd` (pure T - S, no reference), which is the regime-1 (classic
distillation from a stronger teacher) control and is expected to lag at small
gaps -- see the task description.

Reference: the delta term of OPD2 (Heo et al. 2026, arXiv:2607.15161), i.e.
`opd2_trainer.py`'s `eval_gt - base_gt` before centering and gating.

baselines.name: Teacher-student OPD (Heo et al., 2026)
baselines.docstring:
OPD baseline — plain on-policy distillation.

Port of `OPDTrainer._compute_opd_rewards` in naver-ai/opd2 @2dac53fb
(`src/open_r1/trainers/opd_trainer.py:887`), which is the paper's own OPD
reference arm (Heo, Hwang, Yun & Han, *On-Policy Delta Distillation*,
arXiv:2607.15161, Tables 2-3, column "OPD"):

    per_token_signal = eval_gt - base_gt - opd_rewards_bias

`eval_gt` is the teacher's log-prob of the sampled token and `base_gt` is the
student's, i.e. T - S here.  `opd_rewards_bias` defaults to 0.0
(`configs.py:223`) and no shipped recipe sets it, so the released OPD is plain
T - S.

DEVIATION FROM THE DOCSTRING, NOT FROM THE CODE: `OPDTrainer`'s own class
docstring and the `opd_teacher` help text both describe the signal as
`(eval_gt - base_gt) - E_base[eval_logp - base_logp]`, i.e. T - S + KL(S||T).
The released implementation does not compute that expectation; it subtracts the
CONSTANT `opd_rewards_bias`, whose default is zero.  This port follows the
code, which is what produced the paper's numbers.

baselines.name: Constant advantage / self-SFT
baselines.docstring:
NULL baseline — the declared null.  It must lose.

A constant signal of 1 on every sampled token satisfies the I/O contract while
carrying no information from the teacher or the reference at all.  Under the
fixed GRPO update a uniform positive advantage reduces to maximising the
log-likelihood of the student's own samples, i.e. on-policy self-SFT (entropy
minimisation on its own rollouts).

If this arm ever wins, the metric is rewarding "the student trained for a
while" rather than "the teacher's per-token signal transferred reasoning", and
the task is broken.  It is a declared baseline, not a one-off check, so every
future sweep re-runs it.

"""NULL baseline — the declared null.  It must lose.

A constant signal of 1 on every sampled token satisfies the I/O contract while
carrying no information from the teacher or the reference at all.  Under the
fixed GRPO update a uniform positive advantage reduces to maximising the
log-likelihood of the student's own samples, i.e. on-policy self-SFT (entropy
minimisation on its own rollouts).

If this arm ever wins, the metric is rewarding "the student trained for a
while" rather than "the teacher's per-token signal transferred reasoning", and
the task is broken.  It is a declared baseline, not a one-off check, so every
future sweep re-runs it.

_FILE = "opd2/src/open_r1/trainers/custom_token_signal.py"

_BODY = """\

"""Per-token training signal for on-policy distillation (EDITABLE).

The fixed pipeline samples a rollout from the student, then runs three frozen
forward passes over that rollout and hands you, for every sampled token, what
each model thinks of it.  Your job is to turn those numbers into the dense
per-token advantage the GRPO update is driven by.

Symbols used below (all log-probabilities, all at temperature `temperature`,
all normalised over the full vocabulary):

    S(t)   = log p_student(y_t | prompt, y_<t)     the student's own rollout
    T(t)   = log p_teacher(y_t | prompt, y_<t)     frozen reasoning-tuned teacher
    R(t)   = log p_reference(y_t | prompt, y_<t)   frozen model the teacher was tuned FROM

and the three expectations under the student's own next-token distribution,
truncated to the student's top-K columns (K is fixed by the harness):

    E[S](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_student(v)
    E[T](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_teacher(v)
    E[R](t) = sum_v p_student(v) * log p_reference(v)

What is fixed and NOT reachable from here: the rollout itself, the three
forward passes, the top-K gather, the PPO clip, the masking of padding and of
degenerate rollouts, the constant the signal is multiplied by before it enters
the loss, the optimizer, the schedule and the checkpoint that is saved.
"""
import torch


def compute_per_token_signal(
    student_lp: torch.Tensor,
    teacher_lp: torch.Tensor,
    teacher_base_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_student_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_teacher_lp: torch.Tensor,
    mean_teacher_base_lp: torch.Tensor,
    completion_mask: torch.Tensor,
    solutions: list,
    step: int,
    total_steps: int,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Return the dense per-token advantage for one batch of rollouts.

    Args:
        student_lp:           [B, T] float32, S(t).
        teacher_lp:           [B, T] float32, T(t).
        teacher_base_lp:      [B, T] float32, R(t).
        mean_student_lp:      [B, T] float32, E[S](t).
        mean_teacher_lp:      [B, T] float32, E[T](t).
        mean_teacher_base_lp: [B, T] float32, E[R](t).
        completion_mask:      [B, T] bool. True on real sampled tokens; False on
                              padding and on every position of a rollout the
                              harness has already rejected.  Values at False
                              positions are zeros and are discarded afterwards,
                              so you never have to mask your output -- but you
                              DO have to respect the mask in any reduction you
                              take across tokens or across the batch.
        solutions:            list[str] of length B, the training set's own
                              reference answer for each prompt.  Training data,
                              not evaluation data.
        step:                 optimizer step index, 0-based.
        total_steps:          total optimizer steps in this run.

    Returns:
        [B, T] float tensor, same shape as `student_lp`.  Larger means "make
        this token more likely".  Non-finite entries are zeroed by the harness.
    """
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # EDITABLE REGION
    # NULL: constant signal, no teacher and no reference information.
    # Reduces the fixed GRPO update to on-policy self-SFT.
    return torch.ones_like(student_lp)
    # END EDITABLE REGION
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
